newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts end mixed, seek direction from data.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts end mixed, seek direction from data.

text.p: New Zealand debt securities closed mixed on Friday in a directionless and subdued market, but dealers said employment data due on Tuesday could set the cat among the pigeons.
"We've got our employment numbers next week and if they upset the apple cart either way, we could break out of the ranges," said a dealer.
Economists polled by Reuters on average expect the Household Labour Force Survey to show seasonally-adjusted employment growth of 0.325 percent for the quarter.

However, forecasts ranged from zero to 0.6 percent with differing views on whether part-time employment would push up the headline number, as it did in the September quarter when employment growth was 0.8 percent.
Economists said a strong or a weak number could prod financial markets into action.
In the meantime, bills were washing around in a range with a close eye on the volatile currency market.
Dealers said the 90-day bank bill firmed a couple of points as the currency's Trade-Weighted Index gained in early trade, and then took heart from strength in the long end of the bond market.
"There was a little bit of buying in the long end this morning and it looks like some stock went offshore," said a bank chief dealer.
"And there was a little bit of selling in the short end of the bond curve, so it was a bit of a curve flattener."
He said the bond market is poised to move on a clear signal from economic data -- if not the domestic employment statistics, then offshore indicators.
"It's been drifting for two months now so it does require some direction," he said.
